leftEvidence.title: The feared fate is reversed across the generations

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: The LORD answers the assembly’s words: adults numbered from twenty upward will fall in the wilderness except Caleb and Joshua.
points.right: The LORD hears the words, swears that the evil generation will not see the good land, and names Caleb and Joshua as exceptions.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: The children feared as prey will enter; the people will bear wandering forty years, one year for each day of spying.
points.right: Moses says the LORD was angry with him for the people’s sake and that he too would not enter; the children will possess the land.

payload.posture: Both preserve exclusion of the adult generation, Joshua and Caleb, the children’s entry, and a turn toward the wilderness.

rightEvidence.title: The oath excludes the generation and places Moses beside it

payload.tension: Deuteronomy places Moses’ own non-entry beside the sentence; Numbers states it later at Meribah.
payload.title: The generation sentence in Numbers and Deuteronomy
